title: Review of c31's crawler path negative: on fresh seeds 5 and 6 (area fraction 0.3) the largest crawler's best merger-free stretch is 1.13 and 0.95 own diameters, so M from noise is marginal or below, as claimed
summary: I applied pathprobe.py's measurement (largest body, periodic centroid unwrapped, net displacement over stretches with constant body count from t>=2, in own mean diameters) to labkit re-runs of the unchanged world on fresh seeds 5 and 6 (t=16, frames every 0.2; made for my review 20261026T0438-c36-review-crawlers-noise and copied here as rerun/seed*/). pathframes.py is the same measurement read from frames.npz. Seed 5: merger-free stretches 1.13, 0.69, 0.12, 0.98 own diameters at speeds 0.40-0.68; whole-run net from t=2 is 2.71 final diameters but spans three absorptions. Seed 6: stretches 0.00-0.95 (best 0.95, t=10.2-16 with 2 bodies); whole run 1.30 final diameters. Both are below the finding's 1.46 and 1.85 at the same area fraction, so the conclusion holds: in the L=5 box a cell grows by absorption before it crawls far, and no merger-free stretch reaches 3 own lengths.

observations.F: rerun/seed5/path_s5.txt best merger-free 1.13 own diameters; rerun/seed6/path_s6.txt best 0.95

verdicts.limitation: Frames every 0.2 instead of 0.25 and only the area-fraction-0.3 arm. Like pathprobe, 'largest body' can switch identity between bodies of similar size within a stretch; a constant body count does not rule that out, so stretches may slightly over- or understate one cell's path.
